## Background

Bedrock Runtime requests for non-standard AWS regions targeted invalid amazonaws.com hosts, and AWS endpoint override variables were ignored.

## Root Cause

The provider hard-coded the amazonaws.com DNS suffix and never consulted AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME or AWS_ENDPOINT_URL; the immutable reproduction confirmed both incorrect request destinations.

## Summary

Added shared partition-aware endpoint resolution for the standard and Anthropic Bedrock providers, with explicit baseURL, service-specific environment variable, global environment variable, then generated endpoint precedence.

## Testing

Added regression coverage for commercial, China, GovCloud, ISO, ISO-B, ISO-E, ISO-F, and EUSC partitions, endpoint override precedence, trailing-slash removal, and deferred region loading.

## Problem

Cancelling a Cloud chat before its first token did not cancel the response stream for custom transports that rely on stream cancellation. The transport stream was split for telemetry, but cancellation only reached the branch returned to the chat runtime, leaving the telemetry branch waiting for a token.

## Root cause

`observeTelemetryStream()` returned one side of a `ReadableStream.tee()` while consuming the other side in the background. A tee source is cancelled only after both branches are cancelled, so cancelling the chat branch alone never propagated to the source.

## Change

Forward chunks through one owned source reader. It reads eagerly only until the first token to preserve arrival-time telemetry, then follows downstream backpressure. Cancellation now reaches the source with the caller's original reason, and every completion path releases the reader lock.

## Verification

- Added a bounded pre-token cancellation regression that hangs before this change and confirms the original reason reaches the source after it.
- Added post-token cancellation and source-error forwarding coverage.
- Extended the telemetry completion test to pin eager first-token timing and source lock release.
- `pnpm -C packages/cloud-ai-sdk test`: 134 tests passed.
- `aui-build` for `@assistant-ui/cloud-ai-sdk` passed.
- Focused oxlint and changeset validation passed.

## Public surface

`@assistant-ui/cloud-ai-sdk` runtime behavior only. No exports or API signatures changed. Includes a patch changeset.

## Problem

The static Markdown routes did not include content validators. Revalidating clients therefore had no reliable way to confirm that an unchanged document was still current without receiving the full response body.

## Root cause

The Next.js Full Route Cache avoids rebuilding these static routes, while the public HTTP response intentionally requires freshness. The existing response headers did not include an ETag that Vercel could use for conditional revalidation.

## Change

Keep `no-cache, must-revalidate` so stable documentation URLs do not serve stale content, and add a content-derived SHA-256 ETag through a shared response helper. Apply the helper to the Elements, examples, tap, pricing, blog, and combined `llms-full.txt` routes.

The digest helper is shared with agent-discovery so both surfaces use the same validator format. The platform-aware docs and design routes are handled by the two stacked PRs because those routes first need stable static variants. `llms.txt` remains separate because it intentionally has a different robots policy.

- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm -C apps/docs exec next build`
- On the Vercel preview, the initial request returned `200` with the content ETag; repeating it with `If-None-Match` returned `304` with no response body

## Summary

Fixes #38.

When `queryMany` is called with a single query in the array (e.g. `index.queryMany([{ vector: [...], topK: 6 }])`), the Upstash API returns a flat `QueryResult[]` instead of the expected nested `QueryResult[][]`. This causes the return type to violate the declared TypeScript signature, leading to runtime errors when callers index into `result[0]` expecting an inner array.

This PR overrides `exec()` in `QueryManyCommand` to detect and normalize the flat response by wrapping it in an outer array when a single query was provided. The fix:

- Tracks the query count from the constructor payload
- After receiving the API response, checks if the first element is a plain result object (not an array)
- If so, wraps the result to maintain the `QueryResult<TMetadata>[][]` contract

This ensures `queryMany` always returns a consistent nested array regardless of how many queries are provided.

## Test plan

- Added test: `"should return nested array when single query is provided"` — validates `QueryManyCommand` directly with a single query
- Added test: `"should return nested array with single query via Index client"` — validates the same behavior through the `Index.queryMany` API
- Both tests assert `Array.isArray(res[0])` to confirm nested structure
- Existing multi-query tests remain unchanged and continue to pass

## Summary

Two related changes to harden the supply chain.

### 1. Bump bun to v1.3

`packageManager`: `bun@1.2.22` → `bun@1.3.14`. Required to use the `minimumReleaseAge` setting added in bun 1.3.

### 2. Add `minimumReleaseAge` to harden supply chain

New `bunfig.toml`:
```toml
[install]
minimumReleaseAge = 172800
minimumReleaseAgeExcludes = ["@nuxt/*", "@nuxtjs/*", "nuxt", "nuxt-*", "@vercel/*", "@ai-sdk/*", "ai"]
```

Sets a 2-day minimum age (172800 seconds) before any newly published dependency can resolve. Mitigates compromised-package attacks. Trusted-source allowlist exempts the Nuxt and Vercel ecosystems.

## Summary

User-uploaded images are auth-gated content that should not be publicly accessible. This switches from public to private blob storage and adds a delivery route that checks the user's session before serving files.

**Changes:**
- Upload: `access: "public"` -> `access: "private"`, returns `/api/files/serve?pathname=...` instead of raw blob URL

- Removed `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com` from `next.config.ts` image patterns
- `vercel-template.json`: forces private access in 1-click deploy flow

**No client changes needed** — the upload response interface (`{ url, pathname, contentType }`) is preserved, and `next/image` works with same-origin URLs without `remotePatterns`.

feat(sdk): return paged list results so models stop repeating the same page
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

REST list tools used to return a bare array with no `hasMore`, and several schemas (`listCommits`, `listIssues`, `listPullRequests`, …) dropped `page` — unknown `page` inputs were stripped by Zod, so every call returned page 1. That made it cheap for a model to loop the same list until a length cutoff.

List tools now return `{ items, hasMore, page, perPage, nextPage }` (object-shaped lists add the same paging fields next to `checkRuns` / `runs` / …). When `hasMore`, call with `nextPage` or raise `maxPages`. `getRepositoryTree` accepts a `path` prefix; tree listings and large diffs are capped in the model-facing output.

This changes the execute result shape for previously array-valued list tools (`result.items` instead of mapping the array directly).

perf(docs): add validators to plain markdown responses
## Problem

The static Markdown routes did not include content validators. Revalidating clients therefore had no reliable way to confirm that an unchanged document was still current without receiving the full response body.

## Root cause

The Next.js Full Route Cache avoids rebuilding these static routes, while the public HTTP response intentionally requires freshness. The existing response headers did not include an ETag that Vercel could use for conditional revalidation.

The digest helper is shared with agent-discovery so both surfaces use the same validator format. The platform-aware docs and design routes are handled by the two stacked PRs because those routes first need stable static variants. `llms.txt` remains separate because it intentionally has a different robots policy.
